subject: Manager Forum: evaluation handback & cross-team rotation
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: amanda.lee@hroutsource.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Manager Forum: evaluation handback & cross-team rotation

Team —

Thanks for making time this week. Goal: land a consistent approach for the remaining calibration sessions and establish a short rotation plan so no single manager carries sensitive exceptions alone. High-level agenda attached (manager_forum_agenda_v2.pdf) and the working scorebook template (scorebook_template_Q3.xlsx).

Key asks before the forum on Wednesday:
- Review the agenda and add any urgent cases by EOD Tuesday.
- Bring one concrete example where your banding changed materially since peer review (anonymized is fine).
- If you have a potentially escalatable case (IC-xx level sensitivity), flag it to me and Amanda so we can confirm HR presence.

Proposed decisions for the session:
1) Agree on anonymized evidence packet standard (what gets shared across teams).
2) Pick a rotating chair list for the exception committee (3 managers, 2 cross-functional observers).
3) Lock the scoring sheet columns and agree on one override rationale taxonomy.

I want the forum to be practical — 60 minutes, explicit actions, follow-up notes pushed to the calibration folder. If you can pre-fill the scorebook with redlines, it'll save time.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: manager_forum_agenda_v2.pdf (PDF), scorebook_template_Q3.xlsx (Excel)

Folks —

I uploaded an anonymized packet (anonymized_case_notes_IC45.pdf) for discussion. Heads-up: this one has potential legal/managerial exposure — conflicting feedback across two teams and a mid-cycle role change. Amanda, can HR confirm whether we should treat the individual's prior manager notes as input or sealed evidence? If sealed, we need a separate trustee review.

Also propose we trial a "blind initial vote" before any discussion on the most sensitive cases to surface raw manager priors. We can drop to open discussion afterward. That should reduce anchoring effects.

Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Agree with the blind vote approach. I also updated the scorebook (scorebook_template_Q3.xlsx) and added a protected column "override_rationale" with recommended taxonomy values (performance, role_shift, process_gap, evidence_limit). If we can lock those choices as a dropdown the downstream reporting team can automate exception flags.

I want to flag one operational ask: can we ensure external reviewers (when used) receive only the anonymized packet and not the full manager notes? We should make that explicit in the packet standard.

-Rishi

Subject: RE: Manager Forum: evaluation handback & cross-team rotation — final notes and next steps

All —

Really productive set of notes today. Short recap and actions: 

Decisions made
- Adopted anonymized_packet standard (see Drive folder). Manager notes are input but not shared with external reviewers by default.
- Trialing blind-initial-vote for top 5 sensitive cases; rotation for the committee: Marissa (chair week 1), Vivek (week 2), Hannah (week 3).
- Locked override_rationale taxonomy as Rishi suggested (performance, role_shift, process_gap, evidence_limit).

Action items
- Marissa: chair week 1 and run the blind vote workflow (pre-fill ballot export) — due 2027-07-19.
- Rishi: push the locked dropdown to the scorebook and notify reporting — due 2027-07-16.
- Vivek & Hannah: review the anonymized packet IC45 and confirm whether we need trustee review — due 2027-07-16.
- Amanda (HR): confirm sealed-evidence policy and whether trustee review is needed.

I'll circulate meeting minutes and the final scorebook snapshot once Rishi confirms the dropdown. Thanks all for the pragmatic approach.

Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference
